data.title: AM Best Revises Outlooks to Stable for Members of Coverys Companies
data.description:
AM Best Revises Outlooks to Stable for Members of Coverys Companies

AM Best has revised the outlooks to stable from negative and affirmed the Financial Strength Rating (FSR) of A (Excellent) and the Long-Term Issuer Credit Ratings (Long-Term ICR) of “a” (Excellent) of Medical Professional Mutual Insurance Company (Boston, MA) and its rating unit members, collectively known as Coverys Companies (Coverys). (See below for a detailed list of these subsidiaries and Credit Ratings [ratings]).

The ratings reflect Coverys’ balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as very strong, as well as its adequate operating performance, neutral business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management (ERM).

The revision of the outlooks to stable reflects Coverys’ improved operating results in recent years and through the first half of 2026, as well as the forward-looking expectation for the group’s performance to be roughly in line with peers assessed at adequate within the medical professional liability (MPL) composite. While underwriting results continue to be impacted by challenging market conditions within the MPL segment, consistent and growing net investment income has enabled Coverys to produce positive pretax earnings in the three most recent years and through the first half of 2026. Significant amounts of realized capital gains in most recent years have further contributed to overall earnings. As such, overall operating ratios and return metrics have demonstrated improvement.

Coverys continues to maintain the strongest level of risk-adjusted capitalization, as measured by Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR). Through its improved results, the group has managed to grow its surplus in the three most recent years and through the first half of 2026. However, persistent adverse prior-year loss reserve development in recent years contributed toward AM Best lowering the balance sheet strength assessment from strongest to very strong. AM Best will continue to monitor Coverys’ loss reserves and developments.

The neutral business profile assessment reflects Coverys’ solid position within the U.S. MPL segment as the seventh largest writer based on 2025, direct premiums written. Management is focused on improving its core U.S. MPL book while diversifying its business across the health care space through expanding its accident & health lines of business, as well as its international MPL presence. Strengthened leadership across the organization in recent years provide support for the group’s current and future operations. ERM continues to be viewed as appropriate, with a developed framework in place and risk management capabilities close in line with the organization’s risk profile.

The FSR of A (Excellent) and the Long-Term ICRs of “a” (Excellent) have been affirmed with the outlooks revised to stable from negative for the following members of the Coverys companies rating unit:

  • Medical Professional Mutual Insurance Company
  • ProSelect Insurance Company
  • Preferred Professional Insurance Company
  • Coverys Specialty Insurance Company
  • Coverys Risk Retention Group, Inc.
  • Coverys Limited
  • Coverys International Insurance Company Designated Activity Company

This press release relates to Credit Ratings that have been published on AM Best’s website. For all rating information relating to the release and pertinent disclosures, including details of the office responsible for issuing each of the individual ratings referenced in this release, please see AM Best’s Recent Rating Activity web page. For additional information regarding the use and limitations of Credit Rating opinions, please view Guide to Best's Credit Ratings. For information on the proper use of Best’s Credit Ratings, Best’s Performance Assessments, Best’s Preliminary Credit Assessments and AM Best press releases, please view Guide to Proper Use of Best’s Ratings & Assessments.

AM Best is a global credit rating agency, news publisher and data analytics provider specializing in the insurance industry. Headquartered in the United States, the company does business in over 100 countries with regional offices in London, Amsterdam, Dubai, Hong Kong, Singapore and Mexico City. For more information, visit www.ambest.com.

data.title: Union Home Mortgage unveils AI and automation advancements during 2026 Annual Partner Celebration
data.description:
Union Home Mortgage unveils AI and automation advancements during 2026 Annual Partner Celebration

Union Home Mortgage unveils AI and automation advancements during 2026 Annual Partner Celebration

PR Newswire

STRONGSVILLE, Ohio, Oct. 23, 2026

The mortgage lender continues to make major technology investments going into 2027

STRONGSVILLE, Ohio, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Union Home Mortgage (UHM), a high-growth independent mortgage banking company with a world-class culture, recently unveiled an array of AI and automation-driven technological achievements during the company's 2026 Annual Partner Celebration held Oct. 16-17 in Cleveland, Ohio. This world-class event brought over 850 UHM employees, known internally as Partners, together to highlight the lender's year-to-date business results, set goals to multiply business success, and foster connection between colleagues. Most notably, technology took center stage, highlighting advancements made in 2026 and a sneak peek at what is coming next.

Attendees were given an inside look at the next phase of technology shaping the business, with demonstrations of both newly implemented tools and future-focused prototypes. These innovations, ranging from conversational voice agents for enhanced customer support to the elimination of tedious manual document review, showcased the transformative potential of technology and underscored the lender's ongoing investment in smarter, more efficient workflows.

"What makes this event so meaningful is the chance to celebrate our Partners and the impact they have on our business and culture," said Bill Cosgrove, CEO of Union Home Mortgage. "By creating opportunities for open dialogue and idea-sharing, we're able to strengthen our culture and identify new ways to move our business forward. As we look ahead to 2027, we remain focused on our 3X initiative, empowering our Partners with the resources, technology, and support they need to achieve more while continuing to deliver a world-class experience for our borrowers. Technology will be the key to UHM's future, and I can't wait to see what new solutions are developed in time for our next Annual Partner Celebration."

While this year's Annual Partner Celebration was heavily focused on technology, the event also featured senior leadership across all departments and business channels taking the stage to share updates on critical areas such as sales performance, servicing, benefits, employee recognition, and more. UHM Partners also took part in a panel discussion and Q&A with CEO Bill Cosgrove and Sr. Vice President of Business Development Al Blank. In addition to those attending in-person, the rest of the mortgage lender's 2,300 Partners streamed the event virtually across the country. Following the event, attendees were invited to attend a celebratory carnival featuring casino-style games, a golf simulator, Family Feud, a custom t-shirt press, and more – earning raffle tickets to win high-value prizes. The lender also raffled off tickets to the MLB American League Championship Series being played at Progressive Field, as Union Home Mortgage is the Official Mortgage Partner of both teams that played in the series – the Tampa Bay Rays and the Cleveland Guardians.

Throughout the week, Partners also attended individualized leadership summits specific to their department or role within the company, as well as a Hard Stops Summit aimed at examining existing hard stops in the loan process to streamline operational efficiency.

Internal loan officer coaching program Partners Coaching Partners (PCP), which pairs each participating loan officer with a high-performing mentor and an accountability partner at their production level, also held their Fall PCP Impact event on October 14-15. The group aims to equip members with the skills and knowledge to increase productivity, generate leads, finetune the origination process, improve teambuilding, and increase profit margins. Next year, the PCP program will celebrate its twentieth consecutive PCP Impact event, cementing its status as a pillar of Partner development at UHM.

About Union Home Mortgage
Union Home Mortgage Corp. (UHM) is a high-growth, full-service retail, wholesale, and consumer direct independent mortgage banking company with branches across the U.S. in 49 states + D.C. UHM is an in-house loan servicer offering world-class customer service through high touch communication & technology. A privately held family business, with a collaborative culture that stands out in the mortgage industry, UHM Partners (employees) are guided by a Code of Conduct that emphasizes respect, open communication, and accountability. All these principles translate to industry-leading customer retention and satisfaction. Some honors include being a Six-Year USA TODAY Top Workplace and a Twelve-Year Northeast Ohio Top Workplace. Learn more at www.uhm.com.

data.title: Supercar Expert Kendall Gath Discusses What to Verify Before Buying a Limited-Edition Supercar in HelloNation
data.description:
Supercar Expert Kendall Gath Discusses What to Verify Before Buying a Limited-Edition Supercar in HelloNation

Supercar Expert Kendall Gath Discusses What to Verify Before Buying a Limited-Edition Supercar in HelloNation

PR Newswire

BOYNTON BEACH, Fla., Oct. 23, 2026

The article explains how factory records, specifications, condition, maintenance, and production information can help buyers evaluate a special-edition vehicle.

BOYNTON BEACH, Fla., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- What should buyers verify before purchasing a limited-edition supercar?

HelloNation answers that question in an article featuring insights from Supercar Expert Kendall Gath of iLusso in Boynton Beach, FL. The article explains that buyers should confirm a vehicle's identity, factory specification, history, and originality rather than relying only on a rare badge or production number.

The vehicle identification number provides a useful starting point. Buyers can compare the VIN with factory records, ownership documents, and other available materials. Vehicle documentation may also help confirm that the car genuinely belongs to the special production series being advertised.

Production details deserve careful review because limited numbers can have different meanings. A manufacturer may restrict total global production, while certain versions are even rarer within individual markets or regions. Understanding the production details helps buyers put the vehicle's scarcity into context.

Factory specification is particularly important with special-edition vehicles. Unique paint, interior materials, wheels, aerodynamic components, and performance equipment may distinguish a model from standard production cars. Buyers can compare the current vehicle with its original configuration to determine whether significant components have been changed.

Original options can create additional differences between cars from the same edition. Factory records or original order information may identify equipment selected when the car was built. Verifying original options can help buyers understand how a particular example was configured beyond its standard special-edition features.

The article also recommends reviewing service history alongside factory and ownership records. Scheduled maintenance and documented repairs provide information about how the vehicle has been cared for. A complete service history can be especially useful with exotic cars requiring specialized maintenance at specific intervals.

Mileage alone should not replace an evaluation of maintenance or vehicle condition. A rarely driven car can still need age-related work involving fluids, tires, batteries, seals, and other components. Paint, interiors, wheels, mechanical systems, and evidence of previous repairs should also be reviewed.

Modifications are another consideration when evaluating a limited-edition supercar. Aftermarket exhaust systems, wheels, suspension changes, tuning, and cosmetic alterations may affect originality. When changes are present, buyers may want to determine whether the original components remain with the vehicle.

A pre-purchase inspection can provide another source of information. A technician familiar with the manufacturer and model may identify mechanical concerns, previous repairs, or non-original components. Those findings can then be compared with available vehicle documentation and the seller's description.

Ownership history and provenance can provide further context. Buyers may review the number of previous owners, registration history, and whether records follow the car through ownership changes. For especially rare vehicles, documented connections to notable events or manufacturer history may also influence collector interest.

The article emphasizes that limited production does not make every example equally desirable. Vehicle condition, mileage, originality, maintenance, and configuration can create significant differences between cars from the same edition. A strong example combines verifiable rarity with records that support the individual vehicle's history.

Before completing a purchase, buyers can consider the car as a complete package rather than relying on its special-edition name. Confirming factory specification, original options, maintenance, and vehicle condition can provide a clearer understanding of what makes that individual example distinctive.

Buying a Limited-Edition Supercar: What to Verify First features insights from Kendall Gath, Supercar Expert of Boynton Beach, FL, in HelloNation.

Through its community-focused publications and innovative "edvertising" approach, HelloNation delivers content that informs, inspires, and spotlights the leaders making a meaningful impact in their communities.

data.title: A New Horizon for American Lithium
data.description:
WEST PALM BEACH, FL / ACCESS Newswire / October 23, 2026 / ELEKTROS Inc. (OTC PINK:ELEK) (the "Company") today outlined a renewed perspective on its emerging lithium and electric-vehicle infrastructure interests, highlighting opportunities under consideration while emphasizing the diligence required to move from ideas to measurable progress.

A Fresh Look at Domestic Opportunity

A new chapter of evaluation is taking shape as ELEKTROS Inc. considers whether lithium-bearing properties in northern New York, near the Canadian border, may warrant further technical and commercial study. This is an early-stage review-not an announcement of a discovery, acquisition or producing mine.

Why Location Matters

A potential U.S. source, if independently verified and commercially viable, could someday offer a different set of transportation, processing and supply-chain choices. The Company has not established grades, quantities, mineral resources, mineral reserves or economics for any New York property.

Building Connections Beyond the Mine

The Company is also reviewing Sierra Leone lithium logistics and possible introductions to U.S. refineries. Separately, it is exploring ELEKTROS-branded fast-charging locations and potential commercialization of its patented Multi-Port Charging Assembly for Electric Vehicles.

A Disciplined Path Forward

The next meaningful steps would be evidence-led: property access, geological evaluation, processing options, permitting, capital requirements and potential counterparties. None of these exploratory pathways is being presented as a completed transaction.

Management Perspective

Chief Executive Officer Shlomo Bleier emphasized the importance of pursuing ambitious possibilities while keeping the distinction between early evaluation and completed business milestones clear.

About ELEKTROS Inc.

ELEKTROS Inc. is a publicly traded company (OTC ticker symbol: ELEK) pursuing potential opportunities in hard-rock lithium, electric-vehicle charging infrastructure and U.S.-patented EV charging technology. Its northern New York lithium review remains preliminary.

data.title: Gannon University MakerSpace Joins NFI Empire's Project REBORN #001, Using 3D Printing to Create Custom Trim and Badging
data.description:
NORTH EAST, PA / ACCESS Newswire / October 23, 2026 / NFI Empire, a fully owned subsidiary of Newport Gold, Inc. (OTCID:NWPG), today announced that Gannon University's MakerSpace has joined Project Reborn-001 as a technology and fabrication partner. The custom vehicle build is heading to auction at The Red Bird Games in Brentwood, TN, with proceeds benefiting The Brett Boyer Foundation. The MakerSpace is using advanced 3D-printing and design capabilities to create custom trim and badging components for this one-of-one Duramax dually.

Rendering of Project REBORN #001, a one-of-one 1979 Chevrolet K30 crew cab dually built by NFI Empire.

The Build Update

Project Reborn-001 continues its transformation of a 1979 Chevrolet K30 crew cab into a modern performance powerhouse, pairing the classic square-body exterior with a contemporary GMC Sierra 3500 frame, Duramax diesel drivetrain, suspension, and amenities. Gannon University's MakerSpace is leveraging its advanced additive manufacturing capabilities to design and produce custom trim and badging pieces that either no longer exist or have never existed before. Through modern design tools and 3D-printing technology, the team is turning concepts into physical components that help complete the unique identity of Project REBORN. These contributions showcase what advanced manufacturing can accomplish on a one-of-one build while supporting the truck's path to SEMA and its live auction benefiting The Brett Boyer Foundation. Consistent progress updates will continue to be shared as the project advances.

The steering wheel emblem for Project REBORN #001, 3D-printed by Gannon University MakerSpace. The MakerSpace also used a 3D scanner to provide precise measurements to other manufacturers so custom components could be produced for the build.

"Project REBORN #001 is a great example of what can happen when creativity, technology and hands-on problem solving come together for a meaningful purpose. Through Gannon University's MakerSpace, we have the ability to take components that may no longer exist, or ideas that have never existed, and use modern design and 3D-printing technology to turn them into physical parts. Contributing custom trim and badging to this one-of-one build gives us an opportunity to showcase what advanced manufacturing can accomplish while supporting NFI Empire and, most importantly, the incredible work of The Brett Boyer Foundation. We're proud to have Gannon University's craftsmanship and innovation become part of the story of REBORN #001," said Nick Devine, Operations Manager, Gannon MakerSpace.

"Partnering with Gannon University's MakerSpace on Project Reborn-001 brings advanced manufacturing capability and local innovation that help solve challenges only a one-of-one build can present," said Justin Fried, CEO of Newport Gold, Inc. and NFI Empire. "Every component on this truck exists to amplify awareness and funding for The Brett Boyer Foundation's work against congenital heart disease and in celebration of the Down syndrome community."

What is The Brett Boyer Foundation

The Brett Boyer Foundation is a Nashville, Tennessee-based nonprofit charitable organization founded in 2017 by Ellen and Bo Boyer in loving memory of their daughter, Sadie Brett Boyer, who was diagnosed prenatally with Down syndrome and a congenital heart defect. Sadie Brett may have only lived for 7 months, but her impact has reached countless children and families, ultimately changing the medical industry by providing kids an edge and fighting chance against CHD. Congenital heart disease (CHD) is one of the most common conditions affecting infants and one that remains severely underfunded compared to other childhood illnesses. The Brett Boyer Foundation is dedicated to raising awareness and funding research aimed at advancing treatment options while providing support to families and providers navigating a CHD diagnosis. Another mission of The Brett Boyer Foundation is to celebrate the love, capability, and dignity of the Down syndrome community. 50% of babies born with Down syndrome fight CHD. Through fundraising efforts and partnerships with like-minded organizations both in the Nashville area and across the United States, the Foundation works to improve outcomes for children living with heart disease so that fewer families endure the loss the Boyers experienced.

The Brett Boyer Foundation: https://www.thebrettboyerfoundation.org/

About Gannon University MakerSpace

The Gannon University MakerSpace, located at the Center for Manufacturing and Technology in downtown Erie, Pennsylvania, is a hands-on innovation environment offering advanced capabilities in 3D printing (additive manufacturing), metal fabrication, woodworking, and electronics assembly. Designed to inspire creativity and collaboration, the MakerSpace serves students, small businesses, and community partners by providing access to cutting-edge tools and expertise that advance traditional manufacturing into a new age of technology. Learn more at https://makerspace.gannon.engineering/.

About NFI Empire

NFI Empire (NFIEmpire.com) is the wholly owned operating subsidiary of Newport Gold, Inc., a North East, Pennsylvania-based custom automotive company known for exclusive builds, high-performance vehicles, and deep technical and digital expertise across both traditional and digital automotive sectors. The Company has ceased all mining-related operations; Newport Gold is now a holding company whose operations are conducted entirely through NFI Empire. NFI Empire's stated goal is to become the first publicly traded automotive enthusiast company to integrate a brick-and-mortar business model with a proprietary technology platform.

data.title: TG Therapeutics Announces Phase 1 Data Evaluating Azer-cel in Progressive Multiple Sclerosis in a Late-Breaking Oral Presentation at MSToronto2026
data.description:
TG Therapeutics Announces Phase 1 Data Evaluating Azer-cel in Progressive Multiple Sclerosis in a Late-Breaking Oral Presentation at MSToronto2026

First reported clinical evaluation of an allogeneic CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy in progressive MS demonstrated an encouraging preliminary safety profile with no high-grade CAR-T associated toxicities observed

89% of evaluable participants (16/19) had stable or improved disability scores at Day 90, despite documented progression prior to enrollment on high-efficacy therapies

TG Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: TGTX), today announced initial results from the Company’s Phase 1 study evaluating azercabtagene zapreleucel (azer-cel), an investigational, allogeneic CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, in patients with progressive multiple sclerosis (MS). The data represent the first reported clinical evaluation of an allogeneic CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy in progressive MS and were presented in a late-breaking oral session at MSToronto2026, the 10th Joint Meeting of the Americas and European Committees for Treatment and Research in Multiple Sclerosis (ACTRIMS-ECTRIMS), being held October 21–23, 2026, in Toronto, Canada.

Michael S. Weiss, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of TG Therapeutics, stated, “These initial azer-cel results are particularly encouraging given that all patients entered the study with progressive disability despite prior treatment with high-efficacy therapies, including anti-CD20 treatment. The safety findings to date, together with evidence of B-cell depletion in both the blood and cerebrospinal fluid, demonstrate biological activity at doses that appear tolerable, while stable or improved disability scores in most subjects provide a potential signal of clinical activity. Of particular interest, five of the 18 evaluable patients experienced improvements in disability scores, including three patients with improvements of two or more points on the EDSS scale, an encouraging early finding in a disease where even slowing progression can represent an important therapeutic advance.”

Mr. Weiss continued, “While these results remain preliminary, we believe an off-the-shelf CAR T-cell therapy has the potential to offer a meaningful new treatment option for patients with progressive MS, where substantial unmet need remains. We look forward to continuing dose escalation and evaluating longer-term outcomes, and we are grateful to the patients, their families, and the clinical teams who are making this research possible.”

TG PRESENTATION:

Late-Breaking Oral Presentation: First Clinical Evaluation of an Allogeneic CD19-Directed CAR T-Cell Therapy in Progressive Multiple Sclerosis: Initial Results from the Phase 1 TG-Azercel-101 Study

The presentation includes data from 26 participants with progressive MS treated across six azer-cel dose levels, ranging from 30 million to 500 million CAR T-cells, following bendamustine lymphodepletion. All participants had experienced progression independent of relapse activity (PIRA) within the prior 12 months despite high-efficacy disease-modifying therapy, and all had previously received anti-CD20 therapy. The median baseline EDSS score was 6.0, reflecting substantial disability, with patients typically requiring assistance to walk even relatively short distances. As of the September 3, 2026 data cutoff, median follow-up was 4.9 months, with a range of 0.1 to 15.0 months.

Presentation Highlights:

  • Azer-cel demonstrated an encouraging initial safety profile in 26 participants, with no dose-limiting toxicities or high-grade CAR T associated toxicities observed across dose levels including no Grade ≥3 cytokine release syndrome (CRS), Grade ≥2 immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS), graft-versus-host disease, immune effector cell-associated hemophagocytic syndrome (IEC-HS) and no Grade ≥3 infections.
  • Despite documented progression prior to enrollment, EDSS scores were stable or improved in 89% of evaluable participants at Day 90 (16/18) and 88% at Day 180 (7/8). Three participants achieved EDSS improvements of at least 2.0 points at Day 90, including one with a 4.0-point improvement.
  • At Day 90, most evaluable participants demonstrated stable or improved walking performance (94%; 16/17), upper extremity function (94%; 17/18) and cognitive processing speed (78%; 14/18), with no gadolinium-enhancing T1 lesions or new or enlarging T2 lesions observed in any of the 22 participants evaluable by MRI.
  • Peripheral blood B-cell counts were depleted to below 10 cells/µL in 96% of participants (25/26), and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples from 21 participants showed a median reduction in CD19-positive B-cell events of 52.3% at Day 10. B-cell reconstitution was observed as early as Day 42 and favored transitional and naïve populations.

These initial findings are from an ongoing, open-label Phase 1 study and are limited by the small number of participants and short follow-up. Dose escalation and longer-term follow-up are ongoing.

The full data presentation is also available on the Publications page of the Company’s website at https://www.tgtherapeutics.com/publications/.

ABOUT BRIUMVI® (ublituximab-xiiy) 150 mg/6 mL Injection for IV
BRIUMVI is a novel monoclonal antibody that targets a unique epitope on CD20-expressing B-cells. Targeting CD20 using monoclonal antibodies has proven to be an important therapeutic approach for the management of autoimmune disorders, such as RMS. BRIUMVI is uniquely designed to lack certain sugar molecules normally expressed on the antibody. Removal of these sugar molecules, a process called glycoengineering, allows for efficient B-cell depletion at low doses.

BRIUMVI is indicated in the U.S. for the treatment of adults with RMS, including clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease and in several countries outside of the U.S. for the treatment of adult patients with RMS with active disease defined by clinical or imaging features.

A list of authorized specialty distributors can be found at www.briumvi.com.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION
Contraindications: BRIUMVI is contraindicated in patients with:

  • Active Hepatitis B Virus infection
  • A history of life-threatening infusion reaction to BRIUMVI

WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS

Infusion Reactions: BRIUMVI can cause infusion reactions, which can include pyrexia, chills, headache, influenza-like illness, tachycardia, nausea, throat irritation, erythema, and an anaphylactic reaction. In MS clinical trials, the incidence of infusion reactions in BRIUMVI-treated patients who received infusion reaction-limiting premedication prior to each infusion was 48%, with the highest incidence within 24 hours of the first infusion. 0.6% of BRIUMVI-treated patients experienced infusion reactions that were serious, some requiring hospitalization.

Observe treated patients for infusion reactions during the infusion and for at least one hour after the completion of the first two infusions unless infusion reaction and/or hypersensitivity has been observed in association with the current or any prior infusion. Inform patients that infusion reactions can occur up to 24 hours after the infusion. Administer the recommended pre-medication to reduce the frequency and severity of infusion reactions. If life-threatening, stop the infusion immediately, permanently discontinue BRIUMVI, and administer appropriate supportive treatment. Less severe infusion reactions may involve temporarily stopping the infusion, reducing the infusion rate, and/or administering symptomatic treatment.

Infections: Serious, life-threatening or fatal, bacterial and viral infections have been reported in BRIUMVI-treated patients. In MS clinical trials, the overall rate of infections in BRIUMVI-treated patients was 56% compared to 54% in teriflunomide-treated patients. The rate of serious infections was 5% compared to 3% respectively. There were 3 infection-related deaths in BRIUMVI-treated patients. The most common infections in BRIUMVI-treated patients included upper respiratory tract infection (45%) and urinary tract infection (10%). Delay BRIUMVI administration in patients with an active infection until the infection is resolved.

Consider the potential for increased immunosuppressive effects when initiating BRIUMVI after immunosuppressive therapy or initiating an immunosuppressive therapy after BRIUMVI.

Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) Reactivation:HBV reactivation occurred in an MS patient treated with BRIUMVI in clinical trials. Fulminant hepatitis, hepatic failure, and death caused by HBV reactivation have occurred in patients treated with anti-CD20 antibodies. Perform HBV screening in all patients before initiation of treatment with BRIUMVI. Do not start treatment with BRIUMVI in patients with active HBV confirmed by positive results for HB surface antigen (HBsAg) and anti-HB tests. For patients who are negative for HBsAg and positive for HB core antibody [HBcAb+] or are carriers of HBV [HBsAg+], consult a liver disease expert before starting and during treatment.

Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML):PML is an opportunistic viral infection of the brain caused by the JC virus (JCV) that typically only occurs in patients who are immunocompromised, and that usually leads to death or severe disability. JCV infection resulting in PML has been observed in patients treated with anti-CD20 antibodies, including BRIUMVI, and other MS therapies.

If PML is suspected, withhold BRIUMVI and perform an appropriate diagnostic evaluation. Typical symptoms associated with PML are diverse, progress over days to weeks, and include progressive weakness on one side of the body or clumsiness of limbs, disturbance of vision, and changes in thinking, memory, and orientation leading to confusion and personality changes.

MRI findings may be apparent before clinical signs or symptoms; monitoring for signs consistent with PML may be useful. Further investigate suspicious findings to allow for an early diagnosis of PML, if present. Following discontinuation of another MS medication associated with PML, lower PML-related mortality and morbidity have been reported in patients who were initially asymptomatic at diagnosis compared to patients who had characteristic clinical signs and symptoms at diagnosis.

If PML is confirmed, treatment with BRIUMVI should be discontinued.

Vaccinations:Administer all immunizations according to immunization guidelines: for live or live-attenuated vaccines, at least 4 weeks and, whenever possible, at least 2 weeks prior to initiation of BRIUMVI for non-live vaccines. BRIUMVI may interfere with the effectiveness of non-live vaccines. The safety of immunization with live or live-attenuated vaccines during or following administration of BRIUMVI has not been studied. Vaccination with live virus vaccines is not recommended during treatment and until B-cell repletion.

Vaccination of Infants Born to Mothers Treated with BRIUMVI During Pregnancy:In infants of mothers exposed to BRIUMVI during pregnancy, assess B-cell counts prior to administration of live or live-attenuated vaccines as measured by CD19+ B-cells. Depletion of B-cells in these infants may increase the risks from live or live-attenuated vaccines. Inactivated or non-live vaccines may be administered prior to B-cell recovery. Assessment of vaccine immune responses, including consultation with a qualified specialist, should be considered to determine whether a protective immune response was mounted.

Fetal Risk: Based on data from animal studies, BRIUMVI may cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman. Transient peripheral B-cell depletion and lymphocytopenia have been reported in infants born to mothers exposed to other anti-CD20 B-cell depleting antibodies during pregnancy. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during BRIUMVI treatment and for 6 months after the last dose.

Reduction in Immunoglobulins: As expected with any B-cell depleting therapy, decreased immunoglobulin levels were observed. Decrease in immunoglobulin M (IgM) was reported in 0.6% of BRIUMVI-treated patients compared to none of the patients treated with teriflunomide in RMS clinical trials. Monitor the levels of quantitative serum immunoglobulins during treatment, especially in patients with opportunistic or recurrent infections, and after discontinuation of therapy, until B-cell repletion. Consider discontinuing BRIUMVI therapy if a patient with low immunoglobulins develops a serious opportunistic infection or recurrent infections, or if prolonged hypogammaglobulinemia requires treatment with intravenous immunoglobulins.

Liver Injury: Clinically significant liver injury, without findings of viral hepatitis, has been reported in the postmarketing setting in patients treated with anti-CD20 B-cell depleting therapies approved for the treatment of MS, including BRIUMVI. Signs of liver injury, including markedly elevated serum hepatic enzymes with elevated total bilirubin, have occurred from weeks to months after administration.

Patients treated with BRIUMVI found to have an alanine aminotransaminase (ALT) or aspartate aminotransferase (AST) greater than 3x the upper limit of normal (ULN) with serum total bilirubin greater than 2x ULN are potentially at risk for severe drug-induced liver injury.

Obtain liver function tests prior to initiating treatment with BRIUMVI, and monitor for signs and symptoms of any hepatic injury during treatment. Measure serum aminotransferases, alkaline phosphatase, and bilirubin levels promptly in patients who report symptoms that may indicate liver injury, including new or worsening fatigue, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, right upper abdominal discomfort, dark urine, or jaundice. If liver injury is present and an alternative etiology is not identified, discontinue BRIUMVI.

Most Common Adverse Reactions: The most common adverse reactions in RMS trials (incidence of at least 10%) were infusion reactions and upper respiratory tract infections.

Physicians, pharmacists, or other healthcare professionals with questions about BRIUMVI should visit www.briumvi.com.

The full Summary of Product Characteristics approved in the European Union (EU) for BRIUMVI can be found here: Briumvi | European Medicines Agency (europa.eu).

ABOUT BRIUMVI PATIENT SUPPORT in the U.S.
BRIUMVI Patient Support is a flexible program designed by TG Therapeutics to support U.S. patients through their treatment journey in a way that works best for them. More information about the BRIUMVI Patient Support program can be accessed at www.briumvipatientsupport.com.

ABOUT TG THERAPEUTICS
TG Therapeutics is a fully integrated, commercial stage, biotechnology company focused on the acquisition, development and commercialization of novel treatments for B-cell diseases. In addition to a research pipeline including several investigational medicines, TG Therapeutics has received approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for BRIUMVI® (ublituximab-xiiy) for the treatment of adult patients with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis, including clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease, as well as approval by several foreign nations for BRIUMVI to treat adult patients with RMS who have active disease defined by clinical or imaging features. For more information, visit www.tgtherapeutics.com, and follow us on X (formerly Twitter) @TGTherapeutics and on LinkedIn.

data.title: Everyone's talking about Roth conversions, but here's how few people really do them - and why you shouldn't have FOMO about it
data.description:
By Beth Pinsker

You have to do the math to figure out your best tax strategy in retirement, and converting might not be for you

Do you want to pay tax on your retirement money now or later?

There's no hotter topic in retirement than Roth conversions. But for all the ballyhoo, the number of people who actually follow through with a Roth conversion is small compared with the number who hold money in tax-deferred accounts.

The Investment Company Institute, which tracks industry data, reported that 1.6 million Roth conversions happened in 2023, based on the most recent available IRS data. The total amount converted was $36.7 billion, out of about $17 trillion held in traditional IRAs in the U.S. The average amount converted was just under $23,000.

There's nothing to suggest these numbers are changing dramatically. The number of conversions was 1.5 million in 2021 and 2022, according to ICI. Fidelity said just 2% of its 20 million or so IRA customers made a Roth conversion transaction in 2025 an that the number had not changed much so far in 2026.

"People are hungry for it, but the dollars, from what we see, are still pretty small. There's basically a lot of engagement without a lot of transactions," said Rita Assaf, Fidelity's vice president of retirement and college products.

It turns out that while the interest is genuine, there are still serious barriers for most people. Namely, there are a few criteria for the conversion to be worthwhile: You need the money on hand to pay the tax, the knowledge that you'll actually benefit from paying that tax now versus later, and the know-how to complete the complicated transaction.

Doing the math

Running the numbers to determine whether a Roth conversion will be beneficial is not an easy task. If you're on your own with the decision, you have to turn to online calculators and self-directed software programs like Boldin and MaxiFi, which are available for a fee. Online forums and advice columns can provide feedback, but that would just be based on a cursory overview of your situation. You can easily run into walls, which may explain some of the discrepancy between the number of people who have an interest in Roth conversions and the number who actually do them.

Assaf said Fidelity cannot tell from the anonymized data if those completing conversions had help from advisers but that she would presume they did. "I can say that Roth comes up as a planning topic for retirement, and clients expect that their adviser would bring it up - or the clients bring it up," Assaf said. "I have a feeling most of [the conversion activity] is coming from advisers doing planning, more so than it is self-directed, but that's just me taking a guess."

Professional financial advisers use software to run projections, but even that is not perfect. Run your scenario through three different programs, and you will get three different answers. Elizabeth Buffardi, a fee-only financial planner based in the Chicago area, developed her own spreadsheet to run analyses for clients, because none of the software appealed to her. One key aspect she found lacking in off-the-shelf solutions was that they measured for a few decades but not for an entire lifespan. She likes to stretch out her scenarios until the IRA owner in question turns 101.

When Buffardi is doing the math, she wants to see if the client will end up paying more or less in lifetime taxes as the result of a conversion. That's an equation that incorporates educated guesses, considering that future tax rates are unknown, but the best she can do is project the current system through future years.

For some clients, the resulting savings are small, a function of the size of their IRAs and the difference between their current tax rate and their future tax rate. She has seen the difference be as little as $15,000 or $25,000 in lifetime taxes.

"You don't need to pinpoint it the way I do, but I like to give people a number," Buffardi said. When the amount they are saving is low, people tend to balk at the Roth conversion. They don't see why they should shell out tax money now for a small amount of savings down the road.

More often, when considering account balances of more than $1 million, the lifetime tax savings is closer to $100,000 or $200,000. That's when clients begin to take action, especially if they are facing high required minimum distributions later in life. Required minimum distributions can add layers of complication to a retirement plan, such as triggering the Medicare surcharge known as IRMAA and higher taxation of their Social Security benefits. Buffardi has seen the lifetime savings go as high as $1 million.

Tax aversion

The first step of a Roth conversion is to take money out of a tax-deferred account and pay the tax due, and then move it to the Roth account. The best scenario is to pay that tax with cash on hand, because then the full amount of the conversion can go into the Roth account to grow tax-free.

This stops a lot of people in their tracks. Either they don't have enough money or they don't want to shell out that much to pay the tax.

Another consideration is the endgame for the money. If someone plans going to spend down whatever is in their IRA by the time they die, then there's no need to convert. If any money left in the account will be earmarked for a charity, the more tax-efficient strategy is to leave it where it is.

Roth conversions make the most sense for married couples with large IRA balances, because after one spouse dies, the other will have to pay taxes as a single person on the same amount of money. They also come into play for people who going to leave the money in those accounts to heirs. "A lot of the clients I have are very concerned about leaving good assets to kids," Buffardi said. An inherited IRA has to be emptied in 10 years, into a regular brokerage account in most cases, and this generally happens when the account owner's adult children are in their peak earning years, with their own kids in college. "They end up saying, this money would be really helpful if I weren't giving half to the government and half to college," Buffardi said.

There's a lot of hype around Roth conversions, which is why some younger people are inclined to make them, Assaf said. But there's a better avenue for those investors, she said. "Do you know you could be eligible for Roth contributions? They're looking at the back door when they could go through the front door," she said. "Do the math. Don't just believe the hype."
